ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Enterprises are always laid out in places where there is profit space, and this principle is reflected through the spatial cost curve and the spatial revenue curve. The figure below schematically shows the location model of the profitable spatial boundary of a certain type of enterprise (O represents the city center). Answer accordingly: <image1> After the cost curve changes from 1 to 2, what is the reason that enterprises still staying in the AE area incur losses?

matched_variant_raw.title: GeoSQA open-ended question - reason
matched_variant_raw.rewritten_question_text:
Enterprises are always laid out in places where there is profit space, and this principle is reflected through the spatial cost curve and the spatial revenue curve. The figure below schematically shows the location model of the profitable spatial boundary of a certain type of enterprise (O represents the city center). Answer accordingly:

<image1>

After the cost curve changes from 1 to 2, what is the reason that enterprises still staying in the AE area incur losses?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the horizontal axis extends from city center O toward city edge B, and the AE area is located between A and E, on the side close to city center O. In the figure, after the cost curve changes from “cost curve 1” to “cost curve 2,” its position rises, and in the AE area the cost curve is higher than the revenue curve. Then reason: Whether an enterprise is profitable depends on the difference between revenue and cost. Revenue has not increased correspondingly, while cost has risen above revenue, so enterprises still staying in the AE area will incur losses. The main reason for the rise in spatial costs in the area close to the city center is the increase in land rent, so the reason for the loss is the rise in land rent.
